integration.title: Identify the exact hardware
checks: Record the exact ESP32-S3 board and revision, and obtain its schematic and pinout.
Choose actuator types and document voltage, stall current, feedback, and joint-load requirements.
Select motor controllers matched to those actuators and list their control interfaces.

integration.title: Confirm mechanical fit
checks: Measure board outlines, hole positions, connector envelopes, and the usable enclosure volume.
Plan insulated mounts, tool access, cooling, and antenna clearance.
Move each unpowered joint through its travel to check harness slack, pinch points, and clearances.

integration.title: Plan power and protection
checks: Specify the source, regulated logic input, motor rail, current budget, wiring, connectors, and protection.
Review polarity, grounding or isolation, return-current paths, noise control, and backfeed prevention.
Design an independent hardware stop and support strategy for joints that may fall when power is removed.

integration.title: Map signals and feedback
checks: Choose the actual driver interface: PWM/DIR, UART, or a compatible bus; verify logic-level compatibility.
Allocate GPIOs after reviewing USB, boot straps, memory reservations, and peripheral conflicts.
Document enable/default-off behavior, feedback, fault reporting, watchdogs, and any required transceivers or isolation.

integration.title: Assemble with power removed
checks: Mount and insulate the boards; check fastener clearance, strain relief, and connectors.
Verify polarity, connector pin numbering, continuity, and the absence of shorts using appropriate instruments.
Recheck separated high-current routes, signal-return paths, and mechanical clearance.

integration.title: Bench-test the controller
checks: Keep actuators and motor power disconnected; verify the intended logic rails and current draw.
Load a minimal firmware test and inspect control outputs with suitable instruments.
Confirm default-disabled outputs, fault handling, watchdog response, and no unintended powering through signal lines.

integration.title: Commission one supported joint
checks: Secure the joint and robot against motion or collapse; use the reviewed power and stop arrangements.
Begin with limited commands and conservative current/torque limits appropriate to the actual mechanism.
Verify direction, feedback, limits, stop behavior, wiring temperature, and driver faults; record results before extending the system.
